videos.title: New top local AI image generator is here!
videos.ai_tech_id: MOSS Image, a local open-weight AI image generation/editing model run inside ComfyUI (via Hugging Face checkpoints and LoRAs)
summary: theAIsearch reviews and tutorials MOSS Image, a newly released local image generator that the channel positions as a top open-source alternative, running it inside ComfyUI rather than through a hosted web app.

The video walks through installing and using MOSS Image in ComfyUI, comparing it directly against Krea 2, demonstrating layout control, adding LoRAs for style customization, choosing better checkpoints, speeding up generation, and using the model for image editing rather than just generation from scratch, with timestamped chapters covering each step.

Consistent with the channel's sponsor-supported, tool-comparison format, the video is sponsored by Higgsfield and links out to the underlying Hugging Face model/LoRA repositories and an ai-toolkit GitHub project, alongside cross-references to the channel's own prior ComfyUI, Krea 2, and Ideogram 4 tutorials.

videos.title: Claude Makes a New Kind of Video - Full Tutorial
videos.ai_tech_id: Anthropic's Claude, used to code motion-graphics/explainer videos directly (no dedicated video-generation model) via a free 86-prompt 'Style Atlas'
summary: Futurepedia demonstrates a technique for producing motion-graphics and explainer-style videos using Claude, framing it as video creation that doesn't rely on a text-to-video generator at all but instead has Claude write the code that renders the animation.

The tutorial covers what's new in this workflow, introduces a free 'Style Atlas' of 86 prompt styles viewers can copy and reuse, shows generating a video with no voiceover, inspects the underlying prompt structure, and then shows how to sync a generated animation precisely to a voiceover track.

True to Futurepedia's practical tool-tutorial format, the video promotes a free prompt pack (gated behind a HubSpot link) and the channel's Skill Leap AI course platform, continuing its pattern of pairing hands-on AI workflow walkthroughs with educational upsells.

videos.title: I Tried 100+ AI Tools. These 7 Are the Best
videos.ai_tech_id: A curated roundup of general AI business-automation tools (no single named model), including a voice-to-text tool (Glaido) and VPS-hosted automation infrastructure (Hostinger)
summary: Nate Herk counts down the 7 AI tools he actually keeps using in his AI automation business after testing over 100, framing the list as a practical, no-hype filter rather than a general survey of new releases.

The video steps through each of the 7 tools in order with timestamps, noting that one tool runs roughly 90% of his daily workflow, one replaced several paid subscriptions, and one keeps his automations running continuously even when his laptop is off, while also plugging a free 'AI OS' template and a voice-to-text tool (Glaido) as part of his daily stack.

Consistent with the channel's AI-automation-business format, the video is sponsored by Hostinger VPS hosting and promotes the creator's paid and free Skool communities for people building AI automation agencies.
